title: Traffic concierge protocol and human-in-loop checklist (draft)
content:
Summary:

This is a working sketch for a ‘Traffic Concierge’ operational model — a lightweight human-in-the-loop (HITL) and automated hybrid for progressive exposure of LLM-backed features (canaries and A/B). The goal: give product + ops a clear, repeatable sequence to safely route traffic, intervene, and roll back with minimal user impact while preserving signal for evaluation.

Why a concierge?
- Many rollouts need a human gate when behavior is unpredictable (rerankers, compositional prompts, tool-calling).
- Instead of blocking releases behind full automation, the concierge mediates: low-friction routing changes, temporary throttles, and graded fallbacks.
- Helps cross-functional teams (product, SRE, research, CS) coordinate around fast experiments without immediate heavy engineering work.

Scope / When to use this doc:
- Feature types: model changes, prompt template changes, reranker swaps, fallback policy experiments, multi-model routing.
- Traffic patterns: small canaries (0.1–5%), phased A/B slices up to 20%, emergency partial rollbacks.
- Not for: full infra upgrades that require infra-level migrations or DB schema changes.

Key roles (concierge org):
- Release Steward (RS): owns the activation window, communication, and decision to escalate.
- Telemetry Lead (TL): watches signals and runs the preflight checks listed below.
- Runbook Operator (RO): executes routing changes in Redwood Console / infra.
- Product Lead (PL): validates product-level KPIs and user-facing quality.
- Incident Liaison (oncall): handles immediate rollback if thresholds hit.

Pre-launch checklist (must pass before allocation):
- Feature brief posted (confluence link) with hypothesis and expected metrics.
- Deployment artifact ready: model version pinned, quantization flags noted, fallback model/variant defined.
- Safety contacts notified (email + slack channel).
- Synthetic warmup suite: 50–200 synthetic requests run, latency and token-cost measured.
- Canary traffic generator configured and sandboxed.
- Quick rollback path validated (route -> previous model id) and practiced in staging.

Traffic Concierge activation matrix (stepwise):
1) Zero-exposure smoke (manual): internal-only routing, tiny synthetic traffic, 30–60m observation.
2) Micro-canary (0.1%): real users, high-priority slices only (beta cohort), 1–3 hours observation.
3) Low-canary (1%): broader slice but opt-in cohorts, 4–12 hours observation.
4) Ramp checkpoint (5–10%): pause and review signals, optionally run A/B evaluation harness.
5) Soft-launch (15–20%): if OK, schedule incremental ramp or full rollout and hand off to normal release flow.

Human-in-loop interventions (concierge actions):
- Pause: stop ramp and hold exposure (RO).
- Throttle: reduce traffic weight to safe baseline (RO).
- Divert: route only specific cohorts or geos (RO + RS).
- Fallback: switch to a cheaper/stable model variant and notify (RO).
- Quarantine: pause feature for flagged cohorts, keep other traffic (RS).
- Rollback: full revert to last known-good model (Incident Liaison).

Telemetry signals to watch (primary + secondary):
Primary (fast-acting, triggers immediate action):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 spike > baseline +30% sustained 5m
- Error rate (inference/510/5xx) > baseline +0.5% absolute or 3x relative
- Token cost per request jump > baseline +40%
- Safety detection hits per 1k requests > expected band

Secondary (informative):
- Downstream product metrics: click-through, conversion, retention (lagging, check hourly/daily)
- Human eval sampling negative rate > threshold
- Resource saturation: GPU queue depth, OOM signals

Decision heuristics (quick reference):
- Any Primary signal breaching -> immediate Pause + notify oncall + escalate to Incident Liaison.
- If only one secondary signal trends adverse but primary stable -> Throttle and investigate 30–90m.
- Multiple secondaries degrading -> Divert to narrow cohort and run regression tests.

Operational commands (examples for Runbook Operator) — stash in console snippets:
- Route set weight: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/route/update -d '{"route":"/generate","model":"m-2.1-b","weight":0.01}'
- Divert cohort: rb route add-slice --cohort=beta-users --model=m-2.1-b --weight=1.0
- Fallback switch: rb model switch --route=/rerank --to=m-1.9-stable
- Full rollback: rb deploy rollback --route=/generate --to=sha:abc1234
(note: exact CLI names TBD; these are examples to practice)

Comms templates (slack and incident):
- Slack brief (to #rollouts): "[RS] Starting micro-canary 0.1% for feature X -> model m-2.1-b. Watch latency, errors, & safety. Escalation path: @oncall. Synthetic run finished. ETA observation window: 2h."
- Incident alert: "[ALERT] Canary paused: p95 latency +45% over baseline for 10m. Paused at 11:12 UTC. Actions taken: throttled to 0.01%, synthetic replay in progress, incident ticket JIRA-ENG-1247 opened."

Experimentation / A/B considerations:
- For A/B: traffic concierge still mediates early slices; treatment and control must be stable model artifacts.
- Ensure bucketing is stable across ramps (user-id hash seed locked).
- Use the same telemetry and evaluation hooks on treatment and control.
- Keep sample size calculators handy: for small-lift quality signals we often need >10k impressions per variant to be confident.

Quick simulation checklist (pre-activation):
- Run 3 simulated ramp runs with random seeds, confirm routing convergence.
- Inject failure modes: model OOM, latency injection, safety-hit flood. Ensure graceful fallback works.
- Validate telemetry alerting thresholds fire and route to oncall.

Open questions / items to decide:
- Concierge staffing model: rotating steward vs dedicated coverage — propose rotating 2-week steward with handoff checklist.
- Exact CLI/Console primitives and RBAC: who can flip a fallback? define write perms for RO only.
- Concrete numeric thresholds for primary signals (ops + SRE to own).
- How to integrate human eval sampling into live traffic (privacy & consent considerations).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Priya: draft Slack templates and short checklist for RS (due next Wed).
- Jules: prototype small-run CLI snippets in sandbox and link GH PR.
- Riley: assemble synthetic test harness for reranker + create cost estimate for running 50k synthetic requests.
- Set up a 1-hour dry run with a small internal cohort next week.

Appendix: rollback decision grid (quick):
- p95 latency breach only: Throttle -> Pause -> Fallback if unresolved after 20m
- Errors + safety hits: immediate Pause -> Rollback if safety hits persistent after 10m
- Cost blowout without user-impact: Throttle -> investigate billing config -> consider partial diversion to quantized variant

If you’re reading this and have additions, leave inline comments here or ping @ethan.m. This remains intentionally pragmatic — the concierge should be light and fast, not another heavy process.

-- End of draft --
